messages:
Talia Benson: Hey folks — trying to de-risk the guardrails gating implementation by splitting into smaller PRs. Can we confirm who’s owning what for this week? Specifically: (1) policy/schema + storage, (2) enforcement in Optimize apply API, (3) async eval runner plumbing, (4) Console UI + backend endpoints. Want to align before we start stacking PRs.

Ethan Park: +1. Also pls keep it so we can land observe-only first (no blocking) behind a flag. If we have a clean PR split it’ll make the rollout way easier.

Benji Okafor: I can take (1) policy schema + CRUD in control plane. That maps to ENG-3912 / pr_18421. Need Jordan to sanity-check the threshold evaluation bits (min sample size, CI rules) but I’ll wire the storage + versioning.

Jordan Lee: Yep I’ll own the deterministic policy eval logic + unit tests (ENG-3913/ENG-3914 adjacent, but really the policy engine piece). I’m already poking at the ordering nondeterminism issue we saw last time — will add explicit sort + schema validation in that layer.

Michael Nguyen: I can partner w/ Benji on the migration path for existing Optimize configs -> GuardrailPolicy refs. I’ll do the data model + backfill script scaffolding, but I’d prefer to keep the actual migration toggle separate from the first PR.

Brian Murphy: I’ll take (2) enforcement in Optimize apply endpoint (ENG-3913). Plan: initial PR adds gating decision evaluation + response shape but in observe-only mode; then follow-up toggles soft-block/hard-block with feature flags.

Chloe Martin: For (4) Console backend endpoints: I can do the API to fetch gating run summaries + artifact links (ENG-3917 backend portion, aligns with pr_18496). Need runner to persist summaries somewhere stable first.

Kenji Nakamura: I’ll own (4) Console UI states/copy (pass/fail/timeout/override request). I’ll start with the state machine + empty panel skeleton so we can hook data later. Will sync with Felix on which fields we’re actually displaying.

Felix Schneider: I can help define the “gating results” payload we want for UI + audit, but I’m not taking the frontend. Re: backend, I can also add the audit/dashboards UI bits later; for now, I’ll review response format so it won’t paint us into a corner.

Talia Benson: Great. That leaves (3) async eval runner plumbing — who’s taking that?

Ethan Park: Runner work is the big dependency for everyone. We can still land schema/enforcement/console skeleton without runner if we have a mocked response, but we need an owner ASAP.

Jordan Lee: I can’t take runner end-to-end; already booked on policy engine. But I can provide the “contract” for what the runner returns (metrics list, CI fields, prompt-set rev, suite id, eval_run_id) so Brian/Chloe can code against it.

Leila Farouk: I can pick up (3) with Olivia (she’s heads-down but said she can review). I’ll do job queue + worker skeleton, timeout/retry policy, and result persistence model (ENG-3914 / pr_18462). For the first PR, I’ll stub eval-harness invocation behind an interface so we can swap in real call once harness changes land.

Brian Murphy: That works. If runner PR lands with a stable `eval_run_id` + “pending/complete/failed” status endpoint, I can have apply endpoint kick off async run and return `gating_status=RUNNING` for observe-only.

Chloe Martin: +1, I’d like a read API like `GET /guardrails/runs/{id}` with summary fields. Even if we only have “latest summary” at first, we can iterate.

Benji Okafor: Heads up: schema PR will include policy versioning + pin to (model version, prompt-set rev). Need runner to echo those fields back so audit can prove what was evaluated.

Kenji Nakamura: UI question: do we want to show “blocked due to timeout” vs “blocked due to runner unavailable” as separate states? Copy implications.

Ethan Park: Separate. Also in control plane we need a distinct failure_reason to drive safe-degrade policy (tier-based). But for this thread: let’s keep UI PR separate from safe-degrade logic so we can ship incremental.

Talia Benson: Proposed PR order (for sanity):
1) GuardrailPolicy schema + CRUD (Benji/Michael)
2) Policy engine threshold evaluation determinism (Jordan)
3) Runner skeleton + persistence + status API (Leila)
4) Optimize apply observe-only integration (Brian)
5) Console backend endpoint (Chloe)
6) Console UI panel + states (Kenji)
Then follow-ups: feature flags for soft/hard block + override + safe-degrade.

Connor O'Brien: From release train POV, that order is perfect. Please avoid coupling “enforcement” with “RBAC override” in the same PR — makes it hard to stage.

Felix Schneider: Can we agree on a minimal shared response object for now? Something like: `decision`, `suite`, `metrics[]`, `min_sample_size`, `ci`, `prompt_set_rev`, `model_id`, `model_version`, `eval_run_id`, `artifact_links[]`. If yes I’ll drop a comment in ENG-3917 with the recommended fields.

Jordan Lee: Works. I’ll also add a note: metrics should be stable-keyed (snake_case) and sorted lexicographically in outputs to avoid nondeterministic diffs.

Leila Farouk: Cool. I’ll start runner PR today with:
- async job model
- `POST /guardrails/runs` create
- `GET /guardrails/runs/{id}` status + summary
- timeouts (default 20m) + retries (2)
Anything else is follow-up.

Ethan Park: :thumbsup: Just make sure we have concurrency limits so we don’t DOS ourselves in staging when folks spam “apply” during testing.

Talia Benson: Awesome. I’ll update Linear tickets with owners + dependencies and link this thread. Next check-in tomorrow 10:30am PT.

(reaction: :thumbsup: from Ethan Park)
(reaction: :thumbsup: from Brian Murphy)
(reaction: :thumbsup: from Benji Okafor)
